narrationTexts: I'll start by exploring the repo structure and finding remaining `db.query` usages.
Let me look at the db module and an already-migrated file to match the established pattern.
Pattern is fully mechanical. Migrating the 13 package files (vendor is explicitly marked do-not-edit — more on that below).
finalText:
Migration finished. All 12 remaining application files are on `db.execute({ sql, params })`:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `repo/session.js`, `service/teamService.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| support | `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |

36 call sites converted, matching the style of the already-migrated files (e.g. `packages/accounts/src/repo/user.js:9`). Verified: `node --check` clean on all 78 JS files, and a smoke run of a sample of the converted modules records 16 calls with `form: 'execute'` and zero legacy `query` calls — including the dynamic `UPDATE ... SET` path, where params spread correctly.

Two things I deliberately did **not** touch:

- **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js:9,13`** still calls `db.query`. Its header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on upgrade with local changes silently lost. Editing it would work until the next vendor bump, then regress. Since `lib/db.js` says the driver's next major drops `query` entirely, this needs a real fix rather than an edit in place — upstream patch, a wrapper that adapts `db` before handing it to the adapter, or dropping the dependency. Tell me which and I'll do it.
- **`cache.query(...)`** calls (e.g. `sla.js:18`) are `lib/cache.js`, a separate API, and were left alone.
